extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, copyeditors, and typesetters (publishers' production staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Style-and-typesetting rules for preparing and copyediting manuscripts and printed matter, covering capitalization, punctuation, italics, hyphenation, numbering, tables, proofs, spacing, and typographic terminology. Intended to guide editorial and production decisions for consistent house style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of epochs and geological periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of names of historical and geological epochs and periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize names of epochs and geological periods (see entries 'Epochs, historical and geological' and 'Periods, geological, historical, linguistic, and literary' with cross-references to pages 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dash for epigrammatic turn/indicating pause or transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of dash to indicate an epigrammatic turn, implication, pause, or transition in text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dashes to indicate epigrammatic turns and pauses (see 'Epigrammatic turn, use of dash to indicate' and 'Pause, use of dash to indicate' and 'Transition, use of dash to indicate'). See rules for various em-width dashes (two-em, three-era, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Roman-quoting foreign words with English equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: When giving the English equivalent of a foreign word or phrase, the foreign form is to be roman-quoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign words or phrases with English equivalents should be roman-quoted (see 'Equivalent, English, of word or phrase from foreign language, to be roman-quoted', p.68).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of essays: capitalization and italics
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of principal words in essay titles and whether titles are italicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize principal words in titles of essays (see p.37); titles of essays are to be italicized (see p.52).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comma before 'etc.' and treatment in quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to place a comma before 'etc.' and when 'etc.' is part of a quotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a comma before 'etc.' (p.130); determine when 'etc.' should be treated as part of a quotation (p.78).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division for etymology (English system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Division (hyphenation/syllabification) rules according to etymology using the English system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the English system for division of words in etymology (see 'Etymology, division according to (English system)', p.204).

rubrics_metrics.name: Even spacing and standard spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of even spacing and standards for spacing in typography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain even spacing in setting matter; see 'Even spacing, importance of' and the 'Spacing' chapter (rules 239-54) including standard spacing (p.245) and samples of different sizes of spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of important historical events and names
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization rules for names of significant historical events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize names of important historical events (see 'Events, important historical, capitalization of names of', p.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Ex-' prefix treatment in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of the prefix 'Ex-' when prefixed to titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on 'Ex-' prefixed to titles (see '"Ex-," prefixed to titles', p.185) — treat as specified for prefixes combined with titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for use of exclamation point
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use the exclamation point and its placement relative to quotation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Exclamation point, rules for use of' (pp.114–115) and treatment of exclamation point in quotations (p.115). Also see 'Outcry, use of exclamation point after' and 'Ironical word or phrase: use of exclamation point'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of technical terms (use of brackets)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to explain technical terms and use brackets for explanatory material or interpolations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanations of technical/typographical terms (pp.232–75); use brackets for explanations or interpolations (see 'Explanation...use of brackets for', p.162; 'Interpolations, use of brackets for', p.162).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of expositions and other formal names
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization rules for names of expositions and similar events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize names of expositions (p.15) and similar formal appellations per rules on capitalization of events and movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compounds with 'extra' and similar prefixes/suffixes
rubrics_metrics.description: How to form and treat compounds with 'extra' and related prefixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See list of rules for 'Extra' compounds (p.192) and related prefix-treatment entries ('re-', 'pre-', 'co-', 'sub-', 'infra', 'supra', etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation of extracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for punctuation when presenting extracts from texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow extract punctuation rules (see 'Extracts, rules for punctuation of', p.102) and further guidance on reduced citations and quotation punctuation (pp.64–81).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and spacing of "f., ff." (following)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to use and space the abbreviations 'f.' and 'ff.' for 'following'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing of 'f., ff.' (p.250); use of 'f., ff.' (p.100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and terminology: face, font, kern, shank, shoulder, slug, quad
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of typographic terms used in production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See definitions for 'Face' (p.237), 'Font' (p.238), 'Kern' (p.237), 'Shank' (p.237), 'Shoulder' (p.237), 'Slug' (p.259), 'Quad'/'Quadrat' (p.239), and related typographic vocabulary (pp.232–75).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation of 'farther' and 'further'
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on choosing 'farther' vs 'further'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish 'farther' and 'further' per the style guidance (p.106) — see repeated entry for variant forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compounds and capitalization of 'father', 'mother', 'sister', 'brother', etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: When compounds containing kinship terms are capitalized and how to form them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for capitalization and compounds of terms like 'Father', 'Mother', 'Sister', 'Brother', etc. (see entries 'Father', 'Mother', 'Sister', etc., with page references around 170–176).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of feast-days and holidays
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization rules for feast-days and holiday names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize names of feast-days (p.18) and related holiday entries; see 'Holidays: see Feast-days.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of 'fellow' and other occupational compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: How to form compounds with occupational and status terms and capitalization rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Fellow, compounds of' (p.173) and general rules for occupation-denoting compounds (p.171).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures in tables and figures (illustrations) conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of figures (numerals) in tables, columns, and referencing illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns of figures in tables rules (p.225); rules for use of figures, pp.84–88; letters referring to figures (illustrations) in text (p.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Names of firms and commercial entities: abbreviation and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: How to abbreviate and capitalize commercial firm names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviation of firm names (p.97); capitalization of firm names (p.9); spellings for 'Company' and 'Brothers' in firm names (p.97).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of first words in special contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for capitalizing first words after colons, in resolutions, in enumerated sections, in titles and citations, lines of poetry, quotations, and sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed rules: after a colon when capitalized (p.31); after 'Whereas' and 'Resolved' in resolutions (p.35); in sections of enumeration when capitalized (p.32); in titles of publications (p.37); of citations (p.34) (cf. p.118); of lines of poetry (p.30); of quotations when lower-case is used (p.49) (cf. p.118); of sentences (p.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of em/spaces and quads (five-em, four-em, three-em, two-em, hair-space, thin/thick spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and guidance on different sizes of spaces and quads used in typography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: five-em space (p.243), four-em space (p.243), three-em space and three-era dash (p.240), two-em dash (p.240), hair-space (p.244); rules for use, samples (pp.239–44), and where to avoid hair-/thin-/wide-spacing (pp.246–247).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of proof stages and terms (galley, galley-proof, page-proof, plate-proof, foundry-proof, foul proof, revise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and explanations of the different proof and typesetting stages and related verbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and descriptions: 'Galley' and 'Galley-proof' (p.266); 'Page-proof' (p.267); 'Plate-proof' (p.268); 'Foundry-proof' (p.268); 'Foul proof' (p.269); 'Revise' definition (p.270). Also 'Make-up' and 'Revise' usage explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid splitting hyphenated words and rules for hyphenization
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing hyphenation, division of hyphenated words, and lists of hyphenated words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid division of hyphenated words (p.208) and consult the list of hyphenated words (p.197); hyphenization rules are given p.166–97; hyphen leader defined p.224.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for hyphens (number allowed at line ends, use cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: How many consecutive hyphens at line ends are allowable and general rules for hyphen use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit on number of consecutive hyphens at ends of lines and comprehensive hyphen usage rules (pp.166–97).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ibid., loc. cit., op. cit. — usage in references
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of bibliographic short forms like ibid., loc. cit., op. cit., and related reference abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for use of 'Ibid.' (p.215), 'Loc. cit.' (p.215), 'Op. cit.' (p.215), and other reference indices; see 'References, literary' for full list and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of abstract ideas and personifications
rubrics_metrics.description: When to capitalize abstract ideas when personified and personifications generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize abstract ideas when personified (p.22) and follow 'Personifications, capitalization' guidance (p.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of 'i.e.' and 'e.g.': spacing and roman
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing and font rules for Latin abbreviations like 'i.e.' and 'etc.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing of 'i.e.' and similar abbreviations (p.250); set such abbreviations in roman (see 'I.e.: spacing of, 250; to be set in roman', p.53?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma usage with if-clauses and participial/parenthetical clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use commas with if-clauses, participial clauses, and parenthetical clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comma with if-clauses guidance (p.131); participial clauses comma usage (p.134); parenthetical clauses comma usage (p.136), dashes (pp.151,153), parentheses (p.161) cross-referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters in legends/illustrations and italic treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set letters referring to parts of illustrations and references to particular letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters referring to illustration parts to be set as specified (p.58); references to particular letters set in italics (p.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of implication or emphasis by dash or quotation marks/italics
rubrics_metrics.description: How to indicate implication or emphasis in wording using dash, quotation marks, or italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dash to indicate implication (p.155); use quotation marks for ironical words and phrases (p.67); use italics for importance or emphasis (pp.50–63).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign languages and words: italics, translations, and roman-quoting
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle quoted passages, foreign words, and foreign titles — italics vs roman, translations, and incorporation into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English translation accompanying a foreign word/phrase cited from a source to be quoted (p.68); sentences and passages quoted from foreign languages — how to treat (pp.51,75); use italics for foreign words/phrases (p.51); foreign titles capitalization guidance (p.37); list of foreign languages and treatment (p.51).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of 'format' (4to, 8vo etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether book format abbreviations like 4to and 8vo are treated as abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat formats like 4to, 8vo as abbreviations (note 'Format of books...not to be treated as abbreviations').

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing of formulae and mathematical signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for spacing formulae and mathematical signs within text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing of formulae (p.254); spacing of mathematical signs (p.254) — follow typographic formulae-spacing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling-out of certain words like 'Fort', 'Mount', 'Railroad/Railway'
rubrics_metrics.description: Words that must be spelled out in full rather than abbreviated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out 'Fort' (p.94), 'Mount' (p.94), 'Railroad' and 'Railway' (p.94); follow the general 'Spelled out' list (pp.82–95).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of various typographic sizes (pica, long primer, minion, nonpareil, pearl, small pica, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and sample sizes of common type bodies and units used in typography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Pica', 'Long primer', 'Minion', 'Nonpareil', 'Pearl', 'Small pica' definitions and samples (p.233 and specimen sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hanging indention and indention rules and paragraph styles
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set hanging indention, plain and regular paragraphs, and various paragraph styles and indention rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hanging indention defined and illustrated (pp.260, 265); indention explained and rules given (pp.255–57); paragraph types (plain paragraph defined, p.265) and styles of paragraphs (p.257).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings and headlines: punctuation, spacing, omission of period
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set headings and headlines, spacing rules, omission of terminal period and treatment of the word 'continued'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headings described (pp.260–64); headlines of tables how to set (p.230); omission of period after headlines/side-heads/running-heads (p.112); spacing of headlines (p.252); 'continued' to be set in italics (p.63).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of geographic names, regions, and parts of the world
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for capitalizing geographic names, regions, number divisions, parks, squares, thoroughfares, and place-names (including foreign forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize geographical names (pp.2–3); regions or parts of the world (p.3); parks and squares (pp.6); thoroughfares capitalization (p.6); place-names foreign treatment (p.51).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of governmental, judiciary, legislative bodies and offices
rubrics_metrics.description: When to capitalize names of governmental departments, judiciary bodies, legislative bodies, offices, and officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize names of governmental departments (p.10), judiciary bodies (p.10), legislative bodies (p.10), and offices/officers per specified rules (pp.10, 19, 42 for University-specific offices). Also guidance on when officers' titles are lower-cased (p.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations: use of periods, spacing, and omission in specific contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for periods with abbreviations, spacing (e.g., p. M., a.m.), and when to omit periods for specific abbreviations and initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing of p. M. and a.m. (pp.45, 202, 250); use of small caps for p. M. (p.45); omission of period after initials of titles of publications (no), after MS (=manuscript), and after certain abbreviations in literary references (p.112, p.no). See 'Spelling' and abbreviation lists (pp.82–107, 97, 100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indices for footnote references: numbering, placement, sequence, reference indices usage
rubrics_metrics.description: How to number and place footnote indices, what to use for indices, and their sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indices for footnote references: how to number (p.220), placing of indices (p.217), sequence (p.214), and what to use for reference indices (p.214).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign institutions and titles: capitalization and roman/italic type
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of names of foreign institutions and whether to use roman type for foreign institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize titles of foreign institutions (p.9); use roman type for foreign institutions where specified (p.51).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quotation marks and rules for quotations (double vs single, punctuation placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules on the use of quotation marks, single vs double, treatment in reduced citations, and placement of punctuation relative to quotation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotation marks rules cover pp.64–81: use of double and single quotation marks (p.81); do not use quotation marks for reduced citations (p.77); placing of colon with quotation marks (p.123); placing of comma (p.146); placing of ellipsis (p.165); placing of exclamation point (p.115); placing of interrogation point (p.117); placing of period (p.113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of quotations and when to reduce or run into text
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to treat quotations, when to reduce them, and when to run them into surrounding text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotations: how to treat (pp.64–81); when to reduce extracts from authors (pp.75–77); when to run poetry/prose quotations into the text (p.75).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and omission of periods after headlines, running heads, side-heads, and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: When to omit periods after various head elements and end-of-article signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit period after headlines, side-heads, running-heads (p.112); omission of period after signatures (p.112). Omission of comma after signatures may also apply (p.145).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for numbers and numerals (spelling out vs figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat numbers in text: when to spell out, when to use figures, commas for thousands, dash for ranges, round numbers, consecutive numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers commencing a sentence to be spelled out (p.86); consecutive numbers treatment (pp.143,157); groups of six or more closely connected set in figures (p.84); numbers of less than three digits spelled out in ordinary reading matter (p.84); round numbers treatment (p.85); use of comma after digits for thousands (p.143); use of dash for ranges (p.157).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and spacing of numerals at the beginning of lines and in headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing rules for Arabic and Roman numerals at line beginnings and in headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing of Arabic numerals at beginning of lines (p.252); Roman numerals at beginning of lines and in headlines spacing (p.252); omission of period after Roman numerals (in.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of ordinals and when capitalized
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when ordinal words/numbers are capitalized or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinals: when capitalized (p.12) and when not (p.39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of commas and sequences (serial comma rules, comma before 'and/or/nor' in sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comma usage in sequences of three or more items and whether to use a comma before conjunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of comma before final 'and', 'or', 'nor' in sequences (p.130); sequences of three or more links, rules regarding comma before 'and', 'or', 'nor' (p.130).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of percentages and metric symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: How to render percent and metric symbols and whether to use figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent: 'Per cent.' to be followed by figures (p.84); treat as an abbreviation (p.110). Metric symbols: how to treat and spacing (pp.101, 250); list and rules in metric treatment entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of money and monetary symbols spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: How to present sums of money, use of symbols, and spacing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sums of money treatment (p.87); monetary symbols spacing (p.251); rules for shillings and pence (see 'Shillings and pence' entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and tabular work: open vs ruled tables, headlines, setting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for setting tables: open vs ruled, headlines, box-heads, rules in tables, reading matter alignment, specimen tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open tables: headlines for, how to set (pp.221–22); ruled tables: how to set and box-heads (pp.221–23); reading-matter in tables (p.226); rules for use of rules in tables (p.223); specimen tables (p.231). Two-column tables to be set as open (p.229).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders and period/ hyphen leaders: definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and recommended use of leaders such as period leaders and hyphen leaders in tables and indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders defined and use (p.224); period leader defined (p.224); hyphen leader defined (p.224).

rubrics_metrics.name: Running-heads and omission of period
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set running-heads and the style for punctuation and hints for setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running-heads defined (p.264); omit period after running-heads (p.112); hints for setting running-heads (p.264).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph marks and paragraph spacing/spacing of paragraph mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and spacing of paragraph mark and its use as footnote index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph mark spacing (p.250); use of paragraph mark for footnote index (p.214).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses and parenthetical clauses: punctuation and placement of periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of parentheses, punctuation with parenthetical clauses, and period placement relative to parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for parentheses (pp.160–161); parenthetical clauses punctuation (pp.136,151,161); placing of period in connection with parentheses (p.113); use brackets within parentheses (p.162).

rubrics_metrics.name: Position and use of section mark and other reference symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing and use of the section mark and other reference symbols for footnotes/indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section mark spacing (p.250); use of section mark for footnote index (p.214).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of small caps and cap-and-small-caps styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition, indication, and uses of small caps and cap-and-small-caps elements such as 'Note' or 'Section'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small caps defined and how indicated (p.238); use of small caps for p.m. and other contexts (p.45); use cap-and-small-caps for 'Section' and other lead-ins (p.44).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of italics: definition, indication, and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use italics and the rules for indicating italics in copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italics defined and how indicated (p.235); rules for use of italics (pp.50–63) including titles, foreign words, emphasis, importance, species, and letter references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of religious terms, sacred books, and Deity pronouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization rules for denominations, religious organizations, sacred books, the Trinity, and pronouns referring to the Deity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious denominations capitalization (p.7); organizations (p.9); sacred books capitalization (p.25); Trinity and members capitalization (p.21); pronouns referring to Deity capitalization (p.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of possessive and plural forms (including those ending in sibilants and numerals)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to form possessives and plurals, including rules for names ending in sibilants and plurals of numerals and abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possessive formation rules (pp.103,148); plurals formation (p.149); plurals of abbreviations in literary references (p.100); possessives of proper names ending in sibilant (p.103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of scripture passages and Bible book abbreviations and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: How to abbreviate and punctuate Scripture passages and handle spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations for New and Old Testament books (p.99); punctuation of Scripture passages (pp.121,126); spacing of Scripture passages (p.253); use of semicolon to separate Scripture references with chapters (p.126).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of semicolon: rules and comparisons with comma
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use semicolons, including in enumerations and to mark sentence division, and examples comparing with comma use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semicolon rules with illustration compared to comma (p.124); placing with quotation marks (p.127); use in enumerations (p.125); to separate passages in Scripture references containing chapters (p.126).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ellipsis and omission indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for omission indication using commas, brackets, or ellipsis and how to indicate omitted words or passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of words indicated by comma (p.141); use of brackets for omission (p.162); use of ellipsis and rules for omission (p.164).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference short-forms and indices (vol., chap., p., supra, infra, etc.) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on usage of common reference short-forms and their punctuation and numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of 'Vol.,' 'chap.,' 'p.,' etc., in literary references: use of numerals with them (p.218); when they are omitted (p.218); use of 'supra', 'infra', 'op. cit.' etc. (see respective entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of scientific/species names and zoological terms: italics and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to italicize scientific names and rules for capital letters in zoological and scientific terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species scientific names: use of capitals in certain circumstances (p.40) and italics for species names (p.40, p.61). Zoological terms: use of capitals and italics (p.40, p.61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreaders' hints and proof marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Hints and conventional proofreader marks and practices to be used when proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints to proofreaders and marks provided (pp.99–102 and proof marks indicated p.106).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical machines and methods (Linotype, Monotype, Mergenthaler) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on different typesetting machines and any implications for numbering footnotes, leaders in tables, or other setting choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions of Linotype (Mergenthaler) and Monotype machines (pp.274–75); how to number footnotes on Linotype (p.220); use of leaders in tables set on Linotype (p.224).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid run-overs and wide spacing; rules to prevent typographic defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance to avoid run-overs and excessive wide spacing or thin-spacing in setting text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid run-overs (p.247); where to avoid thin-spacing and wide spacing (pp.246–247); standards of good spacing (p.245).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of titles of publications and subdivisions: capitalization and italics vs roman-quote
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format titles of books, articles, periodicals, poems, plays, pamphlets, proceedings, series, etc., including whether to italicize, roman-quote, or capitalize principal words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles of publications: capitalize principal words (p.37); italics for most titles (p.52); serial titles to be roman-quoted (p.70); rules for when to use roman vs italics for various categories (books, articles, cycles of poems, short poems, series, treatises, transactions, etc.) with many cross-references (pp.52, 70–72, 95).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling rules and lists (words with multiple spellings, ages, centuries, names)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spelling rules for many classes: words with more than one spelling, ages, centuries, Christian names, months, sessions of Congress, United States, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive spelling rules (pp.82–107) including lists of words with multiple spellings (p.107), spelling of ages (p.89), centuries (p.90), Christian names (p.83), months (p.92), states and territories abbreviations (p.96), and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of initials and separation of initials on different lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to use initials in titles and the rule against separating initials across lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initials in titles of publications: avoid use (no); separation of initials in different lines to be avoided (p.202).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of capital and small caps for certain introductory words (e.g., 'Note', 'Whereas')
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use cap-and-small-caps styles for words introducing notes, sections, or resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of cap-and-small-caps for 'Note' introducing a note not a footnote (p.44); use of cap-and-small-caps for 'Section' introducing paragraphs (p.44); 'Whereas' in resolutions (p.44).

rubrics_metrics.name: Head and side-head rules (use of dash, lower-case, omission of period)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set side-heads and subheads including dash usage, lower-casing, and punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Side-heads defined and rules (p.261); omit period after side-heads (p.112); use of dash in connection with side-heads (p.156); use lower-case in side-heads (p.48, cf. p.156).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of parallel mark and paragraph indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of parallel mark in text and for footnote indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel mark: use for footnote index (p.214) and other reference marks as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for abbreviations in literary references and formation of plural abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Which words are to be abbreviated in literary references and how to form plurals of such abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of words to abbreviate in literary references and rules for plural formation (p.100; cf. pp.33, 218). Use numerals with 'Vol.', 'chap.', 'p.' etc. (p.218).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of proper names and derived adjectives/verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of proper names and treatment of verbs/adjectives derived from proper names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper names capitalization (p.1); form of possessive of proper names (p.103); verbs/adjectives derived from proper names generally lower-cased (p.46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quotation marks with preface/index headings and omission conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: When to omit quotation marks with headings like Preface or Index and similar subdivisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotation marks to be omitted with Preface, Index, etc. (p.72); treat subdivisions and some headings as roman-quoted or capitalized without quotation marks per guidance (p.72).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic sequences and use of dash in references
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of dash for indicating ranges and continuity in references and bibliographies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of dash in connection with references (p.158) and to indicate omission or ranges (pp.157–158).
